title: Pricing at a school juice stall
body: Meera runs a juice stall outside a school. Last month she sold 200 glasses of fresh lime soda a day at Rs 40 a glass. When the cost of lemons went up, she raised the price to Rs 44 a glass, and her daily sales fell to 184 glasses. She was surprised that the money she collected each day from the soda did not fall. Her stall also sells mango shakes. From her records over many months she has found that, whatever price she charges, the price per glass multiplied by the number of glasses sold in a day always comes to about Rs 6,000; at Rs 60 a glass she sells 100 glasses a day. She is now thinking of lowering the price of the mango shake to attract more students and wants to know how this will affect her daily collection.
